discovery.about: obscura-net, the networking layer: default and stealth HTTP clients, SSRF guarding, cookies, encodings, robots.txt and the tracker blocklist.
discovery.see: ObscuraHttpClient on reqwest: resource requests with type, mode and credentials, redirects, custom trust stores via SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR, proxies, the SsrfGuardResolver that checks addresses at DNS resolution, callback registry and error types.

StealthHttpClient on wreq and BoringSSL presenting a consistent Chrome TLS ClientHello, ALPN and header order, with its own SSRF-guarding DNS resolver so stealth mode cannot reach private addresses, and tracker blocking.

CookieJar implementing RFC 6265bis: domain canonicalization ignoring a leading dot, default cookie paths, SameSite normalization and same-site context checks, expiry, HttpOnly and Secure handling, and serialization for storage persistence.

Charset detection and decoding of response bodies (issue 113): labels from headers, BOMs and meta tags for GBK, Big5 and other encodings instead of lossy UTF-8, plus URL query encoding in the document charset.
RobotsCache for --obey-robots: fetches and parses robots.txt per origin up to Google's documented size limit, evicting the oldest origins beyond a bound.
Tracker blocklist lookup used by the stealth transport: checks a host and its parent domains against the bundled pgl_domains.txt list of analytics, ad and fingerprinting domains.

Operator-facing hints for private-network denials: explains the --allow-private-network opt-in for ordinary local addresses but never suggests relaxing the guard for cloud metadata or special-purpose ranges.
The bundled tracker and ad domain list (3,520 hostnames, starting with entries such as 101com.com) compiled into the binary and checked by blocklist.rs when stealth tracker blocking is enabled.
